classification.habitat: Dry deciduous forests, scrub and open woodland
classification.distribution: Indian subcontinent and adjoining tropical regions

identification.description: Deciduous tree with distinctive trifoliate leaves and brilliant orange-scarlet flowers, often conspicuous when leafless.
identification.whole_plant: Small to medium deciduous tree with irregular crown.
identification.root: Woody root system; root material should be authenticated before use.
identification.stem: Stout woody trunk with rough grey-brown bark and branching crown.
identification.leaf: Large trifoliate leaves with three broad leaflets, often leathery and long-petioled.
identification.flower: Large orange to scarlet, pea-family flowers borne in dense racemes; often appear before or with new leaves.
identification.fruit: Flat one-seeded pod, typically winged around the seed-bearing portion.
identification.seed: Single flattened seed within the pod.
identification.bark: Grey to grey-brown, rough and fissured with age.

therapeutics.precautions: Different plant parts have different traditional uses; do not infer dosing from this educational record.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Butea monosperma has been investigated for antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory and anthelmintic-related activities; laboratory findings should not be treated as proof of clinical efficacy.
modern_information.safety_notes: Use correctly identified plant material and appropriate professional references.

student.quick_revision: Palasha (Butea monosperma): deciduous Fabaceae tree; trifoliate leaves, flame-coloured flowers and flat one-seeded pods are key identification characters.
